newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE SHARES PLUMB NEW 4-YEAR LOWS, SEEN LOWER.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE SHARES PLUMB NEW 4-YEAR LOWS, SEEN LOWER.

text.p: Singapore shares plumbed new four-year lows on Wednesday as foreign investors stayed out of the market or further reduced their weighting in local stocks.
By the 0430 GMT lunchtime close, the blue chip benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) was 16.87 points lower at 1,876.59 -- a level not seen since August 1993.
Dealers said the market did not appear to have an immediate floor and some chart analysts said the STII could slide as far as 1,800 points before rallying.
Most of the 30 STII component stocks were sold lower, led by soft drinks firm Fraser & Neave, which lost 55 cents to stand at Singapore $9.00 by the midday break.
One of the most active early stocks was music disc-maker SM Summit, which plunged more than 37 percent after its offices were raided in connection with software piracy charges.
The stock was suspended late morning after it had dropped 39.5 cents to S$0.655 on volume of more than 12 million shares.
Officials of the Business Software Alliance industry watchdog told a news conference SM Summit's offices were raied following civil suits by Microsoft and two other U.S.-listed firms.
SM Summit officials were unavailable for immediate comment.
Top of the early volume again was newly-listed venture capital company Hotung Investment HOTU.SI, which saw almost 36 million shares traded as the stock fell two cents to US$0.68.
